issue.title: Full-suite run leaks a var/tmp/<managed-root>/opencode temp dir past the leak guard
issue.description:
While verifying the fix for sase-cu (flaky test_artifact_file_modal_copy_palette_formats_marked_sets_and_skips), I ran the full 'just test' / 'just check' suite three times in a row to confirm my fix held under xdist contention. The system-temp-leakage guard (tests/_tmp_leak_guard.py) failed 2 of the 3 runs with an identical report:

  /var/tmp/sase-<hash> (1 new):
    - opencode

This "opencode" directory is not in FOREIGN_ENTRY_PATTERNS (tests/_tmp_leak_guard.py), so the guard correctly flags it as suite-caused leakage. The real `opencode` CLI (a node-based binary) is present on PATH in this dev/agent environment (~/.config/nvm/versions/node/v22.14.0/bin/opencode), which is a strong hint: some test that touches sase's opencode provider integration (see src/sase/llm_provider/opencode.py, src/sase/llm_provider/_subprocess_opencode.py, or one of tests/test_llm_provider_opencode.py, tests/test_qwen_opencode_integration_polish.py, tests/test_xprompt_model_completion.py, tests/test_model_picker_options.py, tests/test_model_picker_aliases.py, tests/ace/tui/widgets/test_agent_list_provider_emoji_badges.py, tests/llm_provider/test_subprocess_parse_diagnostics.py) is not fully mocking subprocess execution and lets the real `opencode` binary run, which then writes its own cache/data directory into $TMPDIR (redirected to the sase-managed sandboxed root during pytest runs).

I did not chase down the exact call site — this is unrelated to the clipboard-modal fix I was assigned (sase-cu) and is genuinely distinct follow-up work. Worth bisecting with a PATH-stripped opencode shim (similar to the xclip/xsel/wl-copy logging-shim approach used in sase/repos/plans/202606/fix_x11_clipboard_test_leak.md) to find and mock the real call site.
